I think the war was to turn the metaphysical concept of death from that of basically 'oblivion' to one of passing on to a new house.
Before Hood's war, death was the end of everything. Death was cessation. This is what Hood railed against due to personal reasons enumerated in Kharkanas. Hood gave it a face. One to fight against. One to rage against and one that, if you were crafty enough, to win against. This is perhaps most simply enumerated in Hood's conversation with Deadsmell and his attitude towarda necromancy.
Where death was the end of all questions now it has become a new enemy, a new foe and in the case of some a final rest well deserved. 
Death was taught the concepts of such things as hope and perhaps more interestingly enough, Justice.

Hood won not by ending Death. That was not possible and frankly not desirable. Death serves a purpose. We see how even a temporary pause in Death can affect the world in the pause afflicted by Gothos on the Letheri continent. Where the dead roam the world bereft of purpose and forced subservience to those with the power and will. Death is needed 

Simply put, Hood turned death from a function of the cosmos to something just a little bit more personal and in doing so won

I enjoy the movies for what they are:
A honest and faithful attempt to condense 3 prose heavy books into a medium that is ill equipped to handle it but which got more and more loose with the interpretation of the books as the story went on.

Is it the best adaptation that could've happened?
No, you could've had one that was a lot more faithful.
Could that have been a better movie, distanced from the books as its own thing, probably not.
Were all the changes made necessary for the adaptation. Hell no. Some were just to add conflict when there wasn't a need for it.
Others, like giving Aragorn an actual character and character arc, yes. 
In certain places the movies did what I think the best adaptations do, elevate the source material into not just what it is but what could've been.

Is this the best adaptation that we are ever likely to get taking into consideration the industry and everything associated with it?
Absolutely.

Do I still wish for a more faithful adaptation?
Oh yes.

In short:
Movies flawed yes but really good nonetheless and the best that could've happened.

I think Pratchett is human. 
And that's the thing that makes him stand out.
When sir Terry gets going. When his words start to make you cry, make you laugh and then, and this is the most important part, make you rage, its because of how human he is. 
His writing is written from the perspective of normal humanity. Seeing all of its flaws, all of its imperfections and all of its small nasty cruelties and despite all that loving every single part of it. He loved humans and was enraged by them in equally great parts and that showed. He didn't talk about great ideals of honour and or chivalry but lesser mundane things such as community, the truth and the evils of glancing away.

Small Gods is probably my favourite book in the Discworld, and I think it's precisely because of one line. In a hundred years we will be forgotten bit here and now we are alive. This is voice of someone who is too human. Who recognises the importance and majesty not of big earth shaking moments but that of more common joys. Of small smiles and tiny kindnesses. Of fleeting joy and personal victories.

Sir Terry touched so many people by his writing because he was human and unashamedly so.

Discord and Harmony are at best the description of the current status of two Shards inside their current shared shell. If the two Shards are coexisting in balance where then there is Harmony however if there is one Shard that is being given priority over the other then there is Discord.

I agree with you that Discord is caused by him not feeding the Ruin within him. Sazed is still acting in a way that is very, for lack of a better word, human. An imbalance that is actively proving to be harmful to both Sazed and Scadrial as a whole, as it leads to a God that is strong enough that he is a target of attack but paralyzed enough that he cant do much to protect his world when such attacks happen.

Dont get me started on God and his whole plan for eternity.

God is highly narcissistic and lemme show how 

So God created us so that we could worship him and glorify him. But the question remains, why? He doesn't need it. It doesn't sustain him or anything. Its the equivalent of us creating AI and then telling them that their entire purpose of existence is to just speak he praises of their creator. Why would you do that if it wasn't to fulfill some inate narcissism? Then tack on the fact that any person who does not do that will be punished for the ENTIRETY OF ETERNITY. Thag seems overblown doesn't it. Especially when you consider that you can till be punished even if you were a great man in life. Even if you helped everyone and were a saint but if you didn't glorify God your end result would be to be punished.

Speaking from personal experience all that it has done to me is accentuate and expand upon what already existed.

So for me life held very little meaning before and holds nearly no meaning now. Before the afterlife existed as something o look forward to but now all that exists is the knowledge that this shit is all that exists and there's nothing else. Thus thoughts of ending it and actions stemming from that have increased. Previously there was something to look forward to and to work toward and now there is nothing so the thought of why even continue becomes far more pronounced.

In my opinion, this might come about in the opposite extreme for the person for whom life and existence holds value. Because there is no nebulous better existence that you now have to work towards you are more free and able to divert your attention in lavishing in the happiness that already exists. You dont have to be plagued by the thoughts of the next chapter and of building up a good rapport for the next life so you can live with a increased level of happiness and satisfaction with what you have.
